hypothesis: Treating click and long_view as ordinal feedback levels and training BPR on all valid pairs (long_view > no_click, long_view > click_only, click_only > no_click) will provide granular gradients for items and give all-negative users a ranking signal, raising primary.
change_spec:
1. In `load()`, modify the `rows_orig.append(...)` tuple to append one more element: `1 if r["is_click"] != "0" else 0`. It will now have 10 elements.
2. In `load()`, modify the `new_rows.append(...)` call to include the click flag: `new_rows.append(x[:7] + (str(x[8]), depth_map[i], num_features[i], x[9]))`. `new_rows` now has 11 elements.
3. In `encode()`, add `c = np.empty(len(rws), dtype=np.float32)` alongside `y` and populate it in the loop with `c[n] = x[10]`. Return `c` in the tuple: `enc[name] = (X, X_num, y, c, users)`.
4. In `main()`, update unpacking for `enc[split]` to `X, X_num, _, _, _ = enc[split]` and for `enc["valid"]` to `Xva, Xnum_va, yva, cva, uva = enc["valid"]`.
5. In `train()`, update unpacking to `Xtr, Xnum_tr, ytr, ctr, utr = enc["train"]` and `Xva, Xnum_va, yva, cva, uva = enc["valid"]`.
6. In `train()`, replace the `user2pos`/`user2neg` logic with three dicts: `user2l2`, `user2l1`, `user2l0`. Iterate `zip(utr, ytr, ctr)`: if `y == 1.0` append to `user2l2`; elif `c == 1.0` append to `user2l1`; else append to `user2l0`. Build pairs: for each user, pair every `l2` index with all `l1 + l0` indices, and pair every `l1` index with all `l0` indices.
7. Leave all champion settings (5 seeds, BPR loss, dimensions) unchanged.
rationale: The streak is at 2, requiring a guaranteed >+0.002 gain. We maintain the champion's proven features and 5-seed ensemble and introduce ordinal BPR pairs. By utilizing `is_click` as a secondary threshold (7s play time) beneath the primary `long_view` (18s), we unlock gradients for purely negative users and improve granularity without changing the model architecture.
gain_evidence: This directly targets the ~40% of users who have no long_views and are ignored by standard BPR, as well as providing intra-negative ranking for mixed users. The dataset mechanics confirm is_click and long_view are nested (7s vs 18s play time), mapping perfectly to ordinal decomposition. Prior runs failed with pointwise multi-task click, but incorporating ordinal pairs into BPR preserves the powerful pairwise ranking objective (+0.0115 historical gain) while strictly adding new valid signal.
ablation_plan: champion_equiv: exactly the champion baseline (train with only long_view pairs) to isolate the impact of the ordinal pairs.
search_check: I am using ordinal decomposition for watch-time/nested threshold labels, a well-documented technique from watch-time modelling (e.g., TPM, KDD 2023) and multi-task learning. I am confident in this closed-form adaptation to BPR because it directly addresses the known dataset mechanics (click and long_view being nested thresholds) without introducing new model parameters, and relies on established pairwise ranking math.
